text:
Potash has been found beneath the Hadrow Flats, the Hadrow Basin Survey Consortium announced on 14 March 2024.

Dr. Imelda Corvane, the consortium's lead geologist, told delegates at the Northern Mineral Resources Forum that core samples from the survey site showed a potash-bearing seam roughly 42 meters thick. She put the recoverable deposit at an estimated 310 million tonnes.

The figures come from the consortium's "Hadrow Flats Preliminary Assessment Report," which was presented at the forum. I was in the room when Dr. Corvane spoke, and she described the results as the product of the survey's drilling programme on the flats.

The report is a preliminary assessment, and the consortium has not set out what comes next. The Gazette will report further as details emerge.
